title: Dissipative phase transitions and chaos in two-photon driven quantum optomechanics
authors: Giovanni Bragadin, Filippo Ferrari, Lorenzo Fioroni, Matteo Seclì, Vincenzo Macrì, Vincenzo Savona, Alberto Mercurio
abstract: We investigate nonequilibrium criticality and chaos in a two-photon-driven optomechanical system. The parametric drive preserves a discrete $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry of the optical field, while radiation-pressure coupling transfers the resulting nonlinear dynamics to a mechanical oscillator. Combining semiclassical stability analysis, exact Liouvillian spectra, and stochastic quantum trajectories, we show that this driven-dissipative optomechanical model supports both first- and second-order dissipative phase transitions. At negative detuning a second-order transition yields spontaneous breaking of the cavity-parity symmetry in the thermodynamic limit. At positive detuning the same symmetry breaking coexists with a first-order transition, signaled by metastability and by an additional symmetric Liouvillian mode. At stronger pump power the mean-field dynamics loses all stable fixed points and develops limit cycles and chaotic attractors with positive Lyapunov exponent. Quantum trajectories in this regime display chaotic-like motion, enhanced steady-state entropy, and delocalization over many entropic Liouvillian modes. These results establish two-photon-driven optomechanics as a platform where dissipative criticality, symmetry breaking, and quantum signatures of chaos emerge within the same experimentally accessible setting.
summary: The authors analyze a two-photon driven optomechanical system to study non-equilibrium phenomena. They demonstrate the existence of both first- and second-order dissipative phase transitions depending on detuning, while also showing that increasing pump power drives the system into chaotic regimes characterized by positive Lyapunov exponents. This establishes the platform as a rich testbed for quantum criticality.
main_problem: The study investigates nonequilibrium criticality and chaos within a driven-dissipative quantum optomechanical system.
main_result: The model successfully supports both first-order and second-order dissipative phase transitions, alongside the emergence of chaotic dynamics at strong driving.
method: Analysis combines semiclassical stability analysis, exact Liouvillian spectral calculations, and stochastic quantum trajectory simulations.
model_or_system: The system is a two-photon driven optomechanical setup coupling an optical resonator to a mechanical oscillator. The dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation incorporating parametric driving and dissipation.
key_observables: Dissipative phase transitions (first/second order), cavity-parity symmetry breaking, Lyapunov exponents, and steady-state entropy.
important_parameters: Detuning ($\Delta$), coupling strength ($G$), mechanical frequency ($\Omega_m$), and pump power (related to $G$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on semiclassical approximations for mean-field dynamics but extends to full quantum descriptions via Liouvillian spectra.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate stability diagrams showing continuous vs. discontinuous transitions, and plots of mean photon/phonon occupations across different pump strengths.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system's behavior by first establishing the model, then using semiclassical methods to identify DPTs based on detuning signs, followed by spectral analysis to confirm transition orders, and finally examining high-power regimes for chaotic signatures.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally accessible platform (optomechanics) to observe fundamental concepts like dissipative criticality, symmetry breaking, and quantum chaos simultaneously. The rigorous use of Liouvillian spectra is key for characterizing open system dynamics near critical points.
